skill.name: web-scrape
skill.description: Extract readable content from web pages using Playwright, with markdown, JSON, text output, and optional screenshots.
skill.summary: Scrape and clean web page content into readable outputs.
skill.author: 21pounder

security_audit.summary: The static command-execution alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline backticks, and Cheerio $() selector calls. The hardcoded URL alerts are documentation examples, not hidden network destinations. The remaining risk is the intended user-controlled web navigation, which should be bounded by consent and URL safety checks.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user consent for each target URL, and block localhost, private IP ranges, and file URLs unless the user clearly approves.
Keep the existing warning and add a confirmation step before using cookies, credentials, or logged-in browser sessions.

static_findings.snippet: - `--full` - Include full page content (skip smart extraction)
- `--scroll` - Scroll to load dynamic content (infinite scroll pages)
**If `--scroll` option:** Execute scroll sequence to trigger lazy loading:
| **Article/Blog** | `<article>`, long paragraphs, date/author | Extract main article body |

Line 38 uses Cheerio selectors to choose article, main, or body HTML before markdown conversion. This is DOM parsing syntax, not Ruby or shell backtick execution.

semantic_findings.title: User-Controlled URL Navigation
semantic_findings.description: The skill accepts a user supplied URL and directs Playwright to navigate to that target. This is expected for scraping, but it can contact untrusted, internal, or credentialed pages without clear scope controls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The usage block explicitly takes a URL argument, and the execution flow navigates Playwright to the target URL. The risk is contextual rather than malicious because web navigation is the skill purpose.

content.value_statement: Web pages mix useful content with navigation, ads, and dynamic loading. This skill uses browser scraping and cleanup guidance to return readable markdown, JSON, text, or screenshots.
actual_capabilities: Guides browser navigation to a user supplied URL and waits for initial rendering.
Supports optional scrolling for pages that lazy load content.
Captures page text through Playwright snapshots and optional full page screenshots.
Classifies common page types such as articles, products, documentation, lists, and landing pages.
Describes markdown, JSON, and plain text output formats.
Includes a helper script that removes common page noise and converts HTML to markdown.
limitations: It does not bypass CAPTCHA, access restrictions, or paywalls.
It relies on browser snapshot quality, so heavily scripted pages may need extra waits.
It requires network access to target web pages.
It should not scrape authenticated pages without explicit user direction.

use_cases.title: Collect Article Text
use_cases.description: Extract the main story from a news article or blog post without menus, ads, or footer links.

use_cases.title: Review Product Pages
use_cases.description: Capture product names, prices, descriptions, availability, and specifications for comparison work.

use_cases.title: Convert Documentation Pages
use_cases.description: Preserve headings, lists, and code blocks from technical documentation in a readable format.

prompt_templates.title: Scrape an Article
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner extraction from a simple article page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use web-scrape on this article URL. Return clean markdown with title, source, date, and author when available.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Product Details
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured capture from a product page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Scrape this product page. Return the product name, price, availability, description, and key specifications.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Dynamic Content
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate scrape for lazy loaded pages.
prompt_templates.prompt: Scrape this page with scrolling enabled. Summarize repeated items in a concise table and note missing fields.

prompt_templates.title: Document a Complex Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced scrape with preservation and validation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Scrape this documentation page, preserve headings and code blocks, note blocked content, and include a screenshot.

output_examples.input: A news article URL with navigation, ads, and related links.
output_examples.output: Clean markdown with title, source URL, author, date, and the main article text. Navigation and ad text are removed.

output_examples.input: A product page with price, availability, description, and specifications.
output_examples.output: A readable product summary with price, stock status, description, and a specifications table.

output_examples.input: A long page that loads more content while scrolling.
output_examples.output: A concise extraction of visible content after scrolling, plus a note about any missing or blocked sections.

best_practices: Confirm that the user provided or approved the target URL before navigating.
Use markdown for reading and JSON only when structured extraction is required.
Close the browser after capture to reduce session risk and resource use.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to bypass CAPTCHAs, paywalls, or access controls.
Do not submit forms, click login buttons, or scrape authenticated areas without explicit consent.
Do not return raw DOM dumps when a concise extraction will answer the request.

faq.question: Can this skill scrape dynamic pages?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes an optional scrolling flow for pages that lazy load content.

faq.question: What output formats are supported?
faq.answer: The skill describes markdown, JSON, and plain text outputs. It can also capture screenshots.

faq.question: Does it bypass paywalls or CAPTCHAs?
faq.answer: No. It reports access restrictions and extracts only visible content when allowed.

faq.question: Does it execute page scripts?
faq.answer: It uses normal browser rendering and a fixed scroll helper. It warns against arbitrary JavaScript execution.

faq.question: Can it process product pages?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers product titles, prices, availability, descriptions, and specifications.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
